originalTitle: Spanish police arrest 78 people in bust of 'one of largest' smuggling networks
summary: The group moved synthetic drugs from Spain to Algeria, then used the return journey to smuggle migrants and weapons.
content:
Europol shared video from the operation, including of police dogs searching cars

One of the largest criminal networks smuggling drugs and people in the western Mediterranean has been dismantled, authorities have said.

Europol said 78 people were arrested in Spain and Algeria in a bust of the network, that is also linked to other criminal activities including "violent robberies, extortion, illegal detentions, and money laundering".

The group moved synthetic drugs from Spain and Portugal to Algeria, then used the return journey to smuggle migrants and weapons to the Spanish mainland and island of Ibiza on "ghost speedboats".

Some of the items seized included 18 high-speed vessels valued at €5m (£4.2m), guns, more than €25,000 (£21,400) in cash and 15,000 MDMA pills.

The sting, led by Spanish police, involved searches in 17 locations in Spain, including Alicante, Almería, Cartagena and Murcia.

Europol said the group had "evolved from drug trafficking into a duel-flow criminal enterprise designed to maximise profits" with outbound routes from Spain and Portugal to Algeria.

"The smuggling focused on synthetic drugs (such as MDMA), firearms, and explosives. Along routine routes from Algeria to Spain, the group smuggled migrants, charging up to €12,000 (£10,200) per person," Europol's statement said.

"In just one trip, over 50 migrants could be smuggled. All in all, profits from migrant smuggling alone are estimated to be more than €24m (£20m)."

The network also provided services to other organised crime groups, "facilitating the movement of illicit goods and people across the Western Mediterranean".

"Investigators believe the network coordinated multiple trafficking flows. Synthetic drugs, and sometimes people, were moved from France and Spain to Algeria, while cannabis resin, weapons, and migrants were transported from Algeria to Spain."

Often, the group used a fleet of high-powered speedboats to conduct rapid maritime operations. This included "ghost speedboats" which are designed to avoid registration and detection, which are prohibited in Spain.

"The group used these boats to organise transfers in international waters near the Spanish coastline," Europol said. "Once the cargo or migrants were handed over at sea, other network members arranged onward transport by land.

"Migrants were often carried in overcrowded boats without lighting or life jackets, frequently under extreme weather conditions.

"Investigators believe suspects perpetrated sexual assaults, physical abuse, and placed migrants in inhuman conditions in makeshift housing."

The suspects were primarily of Algerian origin and had connections to criminal groups in France, Belgium, Portugal, Italy and Poland.

Other objects seized in the police sting included satellite phones, GPS devices, encrypted communication tools and satellite dishes.

The announcement comes a week after roughly 78,000 migrants fled into the Spanish North African territory of Ceuta that was blamed on online rumours about an open border.

Most of the migrants returned to Morocco but between 3,000 and 5,000 remain in the territory, the exclave's leader Juan Jesús Vivas said.

chineseTitle: 西班牙警方破获“最大”走私网络，逮捕 78 人
chineseSummary: 该团伙将合成毒品从西班牙运往阿尔及利亚，然后利用回程走私移民和武器。
chineseContent:
欧洲刑警组织分享了此次行动的视频，其中包括警犬搜查汽车的视频

当局表示，西地中海最大的毒品和人口走私犯罪网络之一已被捣毁。

欧洲刑警组织表示，在西班牙和阿尔及利亚的一次查获中，有 78 人被捕，该网络还与其他犯罪活动有关，包括“暴力抢劫、敲诈勒索、非法拘留和洗钱”。

该团伙将合成毒品从西班牙和葡萄牙运往阿尔及利亚，然后利用回程利用“幽灵快艇”将移民和武器走私到西班牙大陆和伊维萨岛。

查获的物品包括 18 艘价值 500 万欧元（420 万英镑）的高速船只、枪支、超过 25,000 欧元（21,400 英镑）的现金和 15,000 粒摇头丸。

这次行动由西班牙警方牵头，在西班牙 17 个地点进行了搜查，包括阿利坎特、阿尔梅里亚、卡塔赫纳和穆尔西亚。

欧洲刑警组织表示，该团伙已“从贩毒演变成一个双流犯罪企业，旨在实现利润最大化”，出境路线从西班牙和葡萄牙到阿尔及利亚。

欧洲刑警组织的声明称：“走私活动主要集中在合成毒品（如摇头丸）、枪支和爆炸物。沿着从阿尔及利亚到西班牙的常规路线，该团伙偷运移民，每人收费高达 12,000 欧元（10,200 英镑）。”

“仅仅一次旅行，就有超过 50 名移民被偷运。总而言之，仅偷运移民带来的利润估计就超过 2400 万欧元（2000 万英镑）。”

该网络还向其他有组织犯罪集团提供服务，“为非法货物和人员在西地中海的流动提供便利”。

“调查人员认为，该网络协调了多个贩运流。合成毒品，有时还有人口，从法国和西班牙运往阿尔及利亚，而大麻脂、武器和移民则从阿尔及利亚运往西班牙。”

该组织经常使用大功率快艇舰队进行快速海上行动。其中包括旨在避免注册和检测的“幽灵快艇”，这在西班牙是被禁止的。

欧洲刑警组织表示：“该组织利用这些船只在西班牙海岸线附近的国际水域组织转运。” “一旦货物或移民在海上移交，其他网络成员就会安排陆路继续运输。

“移民经常乘坐拥挤的船只，没有照明设备或救生衣，而且经常在极端天气条件下进行。

“调查人员认为，嫌疑人实施了性侵犯、身体虐待，并将移民安置在临时住房中，使其处于不人道的条件下。”

这些嫌疑人主要是阿尔及利亚裔，与法国、比利时、葡萄牙、意大利和波兰的犯罪集团有联系。

警方在这次行动中查获的其他物品包括卫星电话、GPS 设备、加密通讯工具和卫星天线。

这一消息发布一周前，大约有 78,000 名移民逃入西班牙北非领土休达，人们将此归咎于网上关于开放边境的谣言。

该飞地领导人胡安·赫苏斯·维瓦斯 (Juan Jesús Vivas) 表示，大多数移民返回摩洛哥，但仍有 3,000 至 5,000 人留在该领土。
